{{Current events header|2016|03|30}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)]]
**Blasts and gunfire are reported in [[Tripoli]]. [http://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security-idUSKCN0WW01A (Reuters)]
*[[Naxalite–Maoist insurgency]]
**At least seven [[Central Reserve Police Force]] (CRPF) personnel are killed in an [[Improvised explosive device|IED]] attack on their vehicle in the [[India|Indian]] state of [[Chhattisgarh]]'s [[Dantewada district]]. [[Naxalite]] insurgents are suspected to have been behind the attack. [http://www.ibtimes.co.in/7-crpf-jawans-killed-suspected-maoist-attack-672725 (''International Business Times'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Taiwan]]ese electronics company [[Foxconn]] agrees to buy 60% of the [[Japan]]ese [[Sharp Corporation]] for 389 billion yen ($3.5 billion). [http://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-03-30/foxconn-group-says-taking-control-of-sharp-in-reduced-buyout (Bloomberg)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Thailand]] and neighbouring countries suffer from the worst [[drought]] in decades as an [[El Niño]]-induced water shortage reduces reservoirs to critical levels. [http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2016/03/thailand-hit-worst-drought-decades-160330102123735.html (''Al Jazeera'')]

;International relations
*The Wallenberg family files an application to formally declare [[Sweden|Swedish]] diplomat [[Raoul Wallenberg]] to be dead. Wallenberg saved the lives of thousands of Jews in [[World War II]] only to disappear at the hands of the [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] forces. [http://www.timesofisrael.com/raoul-wallenberg-to-be-officially-declared-dead-by-sweden/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
**The [[Verkhovna Rada|Ukrainian parliament]] votes to ban all [[Russia|Russian]] films released after January 1, 2014, saying the move is aimed at improving “national security"; more than 430 Russian films and TV series fall under the new measures. Last month, the [[State Committee in Television and Radio-broadcasting (Ukraine)|State Committee in Television and Radio-broadcasting]] in [[Ukraine]] removed 15 Russian TV channels from being broadcast in Ukraine. [https://www.rt.com/news/337728-ukraine-bans-russian-movies/ (RT)]

;Law and crime
*A [[Bangladesh]] Court issues an arrest warrant, the second one so far, for former [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|Prime Minister]] [[Khaleda Zia]] and 27 opposition [[Bangladesh Nationalist Party]] members over political violence, mostly petrol-bomb attacks, that occurred during anti-government protests last year that killed at least 120 people. [http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2016/03/bangladesh-arrest-warrant-issued-pm-160330125529350.html (''Al Jazeera'')] 

;Politics and elections
*[[Myanmar general election, 2015]]
**In [[Myanmar|Myanmar's]] capital [[Naypyidaw]], [[Htin Kyaw]] is sworn in by House Speaker [[Mahn Win Khaing Than]] as the first civilian president in 54 years.  Htin Kyaw, a close aide to [[Aung San Suu Kyi]], takes power from former general [[Thein Sein]]. [http://www.dailymail.co.uk/wires/afp/article-3515031/Suu-Kyi-aide-sworn-Myanmar-president-historic-power-shift.html (''Daily Mail'')]
*The government of [[Pakistan]] warns that it will push to clear the [[Islamism|Islamist]] protests occurring in [[Islamabad]]. Protests have broken out in the capital and other cities ever since [[Mumtaz Qadri]] was executed last February for his role in killing [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]] governor [[Salmaan Taseer]] in 2011 because he opposed Pakistan's blasphemy laws. [http://www.rferl.org/content/pakistan-warns-will-clear-islamic-protesters-islamabad-/27643397.html (Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty)]
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)]]
**The [[United Nations]]-backed [[Presidential Council (Libya)|Libyan Presidential Council]] arrives in [[Tripoli]] despite warnings by hardliners opposed to any unity government that they will attempt to keep them out of the city. [http://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/mar/30/libyan-presidential-council-unity-government-fayez-sarraj-tripoli (''The Guardian'')]
*The opposition controlled [[National Assembly (Venezuela)|National Assembly]] of [[Venezuela]] passes an amnesty bill that could potentially free over 70 opposition leaders and activists jailed during [[2014–16 Venezuelan protests|protests]] last year, including prominent leader [[Leopoldo López]]. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-35924647 (BBC)]

;Sports
*Two [[Russian people|Russian]] cyclists, former world champion [[Anastasia Chulkova]] and [[Pavel Yakushevskiy]], test positive for [[meldonium]]. [http://bigstory.ap.org/article/8f7ca5f04a454bfda94997714769f13c/russia-says-2-cyclists-have-tested-positive-meldoniun (AP)]
*Three-time [[Kentucky Derby]] winning jockey [[Calvin Borel]] announces his retirement. [http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/horses/triple/derby/2016/03/30/videos--jockey-calvin-borels-memorable-moments/82434194/ (''Louisville Courier-Journal'')]
